1-01.title: 上 / 上边
1-01.meaning: 上 means on or on top of something.
1-01.placement: Put it after the noun for the thing, usually after 在.
1-01.english_note: English says "on" before the noun, but Chinese puts 上 after it.
1-01.text: 上 means on or on top of something. Put it after the noun for the thing, usually after 在. English says "on" before the noun, but Chinese puts 上 after it.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing location with "zai... shang / xia / li" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGFBWZL)

1-01.title: 下 / 下边
structure: Noun + 在 + Noun + 下 / 下边
1-01.meaning: 下 means under or below something.
1-01.placement: Put it after the noun for the thing, usually after 在.
1-01.english_note: English says "under" before the noun, but Chinese puts 下 after it.
1-01.text: 下 means under or below something. Put it after the noun for the thing, usually after 在. English says "under" before the noun, but Chinese puts 下 after it.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing location with "zai... shang / xia / li" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGFBWZL)

1-01.title: 里 / 里边
1-01.meaning: 里 means in or inside something.
1-01.placement: Put it after the noun for the place or container, usually after 在.
1-01.english_note: English says "in" before the noun, but Chinese puts 里 after it.
1-01.text: 里 means in or inside something. Put it after the noun for the place or container, usually after 在. English says "in" before the noun, but Chinese puts 里 after it.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing location with "zai... shang / xia / li" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGFBWZL)

1-02.title: 会
structure: Subj. + 会 + Verb + Obj. + 吗?
1-02.meaning: 会 means can, or knowing how to do something you learned.
1-02.text: 会 means can, or knowing how to do something you learned. Put it before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing ability or possibility with "neng" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG9PQ40)
AllSet Learning: Expressing a learned skill with "hui" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGRHM0E)

1-02.title: 能
1-02.meaning: 能 means can, when something is possible or allowed.
1-02.text: 能 means can, when something is possible or allowed. Put it before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing ability or possibility with "neng" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG9PQ40)
AllSet Learning: Expressing a learned skill with "hui" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGRHM0E)

1-03.title: 想
1-03.meaning: 想 means want to or would like to do something.
1-03.english_note: The verb comes right after 想, with no word for "to".
1-03.text: 想 means want to or would like to do something. The verb comes right after 想, with no word for "to".
sources: AllSet Learning: Auxiliary verb "yao" and its multiple meanings (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG95AL1)
AllSet Learning: Expressing "would like to" with "xiang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGT97VF)

1-03.title: 要
1-03.meaning: 要 means want something or want to do something, and it can also mean will or need to.
1-03.placement: Put 要 after the subject, before the noun or verb.
1-03.english_note: The verb comes right after 要, with no word for "to".
1-03.text: 要 means want something or want to do something, and it can also mean will or need to. Put 要 after the subject, before the noun or verb. The verb comes right after 要, with no word for "to".
sources: AllSet Learning: Auxiliary verb "yao" and its multiple meanings (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG95AL1)
AllSet Learning: Expressing "would like to" with "xiang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGT97VF)

1-04.title: 谁
1-04.meaning: 谁 means "who", and 谁的 means "whose".
1-04.placement: Put it where the answer would go.
1-04.english_note: The question word stays in the same place as the answer, not at the front.
1-04.text: 谁 means "who", and 谁的 means "whose". Put it where the answer would go. The question word stays in the same place as the answer, not at the front.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)
AllSet Learning: How to do something with "zenme" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGH2MNO)

1-04.title: 几
1-04.meaning: 几 means "how many" and is used for small numbers like the time, the date and age.
1-04.placement: Put it where the number would go, before a word like 点, 月, 日 or 岁.
1-04.english_note: Where English says "what time" or "how old", Chinese just uses 几.
1-04.text: 几 means "how many" and is used for small numbers like the time, the date and age. Put it where the number would go, before a word like 点, 月, 日 or 岁. Where English says "what time" or "how old", Chinese just uses 几.

AllSet Learning: How to do something with "zenme" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGH2MNO)

1-04.title: 什么
1-04.placement: Put it where the answer would go.
1-04.english_note: The question word stays in the same place as the answer, not at the front.
1-04.text: 什么 means "what". Put it where the answer would go. The question word stays in the same place as the answer, not at the front.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)
AllSet Learning: How to do something with "zenme" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGH2MNO)

1-04.title: 哪
1-04.placement: Put it before a measure word, such as 个.
1-04.text: 哪 means "which". Put it before a measure word, such as 个.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)
AllSet Learning: How to do something with "zenme" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGH2MNO)

1-04.title: 哪些
1-04.meaning: 哪些 means "which ones" and asks about more than one thing.
1-04.placement: Put it where the answer would go, often before the verb.
1-04.text: 哪些 means "which ones" and asks about more than one thing. Put it where the answer would go, often before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)
AllSet Learning: How to do something with "zenme" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGH2MNO)

1-04.title: 怎么
1-04.meaning: 怎么 means "how" and asks in what way something is done.
1-04.placement: Put it right before the verb.
1-04.english_note: English starts with "how", but Chinese puts 怎么 just before the verb.
1-04.text: 怎么 means "how" and asks in what way something is done. Put it right before the verb. English starts with "how", but Chinese puts 怎么 just before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)
AllSet Learning: How to do something with "zenme" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGH2MNO)

1-04.title: 多少
1-04.meaning: 多少 means "how many" or "how much" and asks about an amount.
1-04.placement: Put it where the amount would go, such as before 钱.
1-04.english_note: To ask a price, Chinese puts 多少 before 钱 and has no word for "is".
1-04.text: 多少 means "how many" or "how much" and asks about an amount. Put it where the amount would go, such as before 钱. To ask a price, Chinese puts 多少 before 钱 and has no word for "is".
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)
AllSet Learning: How to do something with "zenme" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGH2MNO)

1-04.title: 哪里 / 哪儿
1-04.placement: Put it where the place would go, for example after 在.
1-04.english_note: English puts "where" first, but Chinese puts 哪里 at the end.
1-04.text: 哪里 means "where". Put it where the place would go, for example after 在. English puts "where" first, but Chinese puts 哪里 at the end.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)
AllSet Learning: How to do something with "zenme" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGH2MNO)

1-05.title: 我
1-05.meaning: 我 means I, me, or my.
1-05.placement: Put it before a verb to say what you do, or before a family word to say 'my'.
1-05.english_note: No 的 is needed between 我 and a family word.
1-05.text: 我 means I, me, or my. Put it before a verb to say what you do, or before a family word to say 'my'. No 的 is needed between 我 and a family word.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing close possession without "de" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGCI0KG)

1-05.title: 你
1-05.meaning: 你 means you, for one person.
1-05.placement: It goes before a verb as the subject, or after a verb as the object.
1-05.english_note: 你 stays the same as subject or object.
1-05.text: 你 means you, for one person. It goes before a verb as the subject, or after a verb as the object. 你 stays the same as subject or object.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing close possession without "de" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGCI0KG)

1-05.title: 您
1-05.meaning: 您 means you, said politely to one person.
1-05.placement: Use it for someone you respect, such as a teacher.
1-05.text: 您 means you, said politely to one person. Use it for someone you respect, such as a teacher.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing close possession without "de" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGCI0KG)

1-05.title: 他
1-05.placement: It goes where the subject goes, before the verb.
1-05.text: 他 means he or him. It goes where the subject goes, before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing close possession without "de" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGCI0KG)

1-05.title: 她
1-05.placement: It goes where the subject goes, before the verb.
1-05.text: 她 means she or her. It goes where the subject goes, before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing close possession without "de" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGCI0KG)

1-05.title: 我们
1-05.meaning: 我们 means we or us.
1-05.placement: It goes where the subject goes, before the verb.
1-05.text: 我们 means we or us. It goes where the subject goes, before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing close possession without "de" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGCI0KG)

1-06.title: 这 / 那
1-06.meaning: 这 means this, and 那 means that.
1-06.placement: Put it at the start of the sentence, before 是.
1-06.text: 这 means this, and 那 means that. Put it at the start of the sentence, before 是.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words with "this" and "that" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGZC42B)

1-06.title: 这个 / 那个
1-06.meaning: 这个 means this one, and 那个 means that one.
1-06.placement: It can stand alone as the subject, or go right before a noun.
1-06.text: 这个 means this one, and 那个 means that one. It can stand alone as the subject, or go right before a noun.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words with "this" and "that" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGZC42B)

1-06.title: 这 / 那 + Measure word + Noun
structure: 这 / 那 + Measure word + Noun
1-06.meaning: 这 / 那 + Measure word + Noun means "this ..." or "that ..." for a specific thing.
1-06.english_note: Chinese puts a measure word between 这 / 那 and the noun.
1-06.text: 这 / 那 + Measure word + Noun means "this ..." or "that ..." for a specific thing. Chinese puts a measure word between 这 / 那 and the noun.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words with "this" and "that" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGZC42B)

1-06.title: 这里 / 那里
1-06.meaning: 这里 means here, and 那里 means there.
1-06.placement: Put it at the start of the sentence to say where something is.
1-06.text: 这里 means here, and 那里 means there. Put it at the start of the sentence to say where something is.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words with "this" and "that" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGZC42B)

1-07.title: Number + Measure word + Noun
structure: Subj. + Verb + Number + Measure word + Noun
1-07.meaning: Number + Measure word + Noun tells how many things or people there are.
1-07.placement: Put the number right before the measure word, and the noun after it.
1-07.english_note: Chinese puts a measure word between the number and the noun.
1-07.text: Number + Measure word + Noun tells how many things or people there are. Put the number right before the measure word, and the noun after it. Chinese puts a measure word between the number and the noun.

1-07.title: 两
1-07.meaning: 两 means two when you count things.
1-07.placement: It goes before a measure word, where 二 is not used.
1-07.text: 两 means two when you count things. It goes before a measure word, where 二 is not used.

1-08.title: 个
1-08.meaning: 个 means one item or person; it is the most common measure word and goes with many nouns.
1-08.placement: Put it after a number or 这 and before the noun.
1-08.english_note: Chinese needs a measure word between the number and the noun, but English doesn't.
1-08.text: 个 means one item or person; it is the most common measure word and goes with many nouns. Put it after a number or 这 and before the noun. Chinese needs a measure word between the number and the noun, but English doesn't.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words for counting (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG64BTE)

1-08.title: 块
1-08.meaning: 块 means yuan, the basic unit of Chinese money.
1-08.placement: Put it after the number; 钱 can follow it.
1-08.text: 块 means yuan, the basic unit of Chinese money. Put it after the number; 钱 can follow it.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words for counting (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG64BTE)

1-08.title: 家
1-08.meaning: 家 is the measure word for shops, restaurants and other businesses.
1-08.placement: Put it after a number and before the noun.
1-08.english_note: English says "a shop"; Chinese puts 家 between the number and the noun.
1-08.text: 家 is the measure word for shops, restaurants and other businesses. Put it after a number and before the noun. English says "a shop"; Chinese puts 家 between the number and the noun.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words for counting (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG64BTE)

1-08.title: 本
1-08.meaning: 本 is the measure word for books and notebooks.
1-08.placement: Put it after a number or 这 and before the noun.
1-08.english_note: Chinese needs 本 between the number and the book; English doesn't.
1-08.text: 本 is the measure word for books and notebooks. Put it after a number or 这 and before the noun. Chinese needs 本 between the number and the book; English doesn't.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words for counting (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG64BTE)

1-08.title: 杯
1-08.meaning: 杯 means cup or glass and counts drinks.
1-08.placement: Put it after a number or 这 and before the drink.
1-08.english_note: It is like "a cup of" in English, but Chinese doesn't need a word for "of".
1-08.text: 杯 means cup or glass and counts drinks. Put it after a number or 这 and before the drink. It is like "a cup of" in English, but Chinese doesn't need a word for "of".
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words for counting (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG64BTE)

1-09.title: 太
1-09.meaning: 太 means too, or very much.
1-09.placement: Put 太 before an adjective, and 了 usually comes at the end.
1-09.text: 太 means too, or very much. Put 太 before an adjective, and 了 usually comes at the end.

1-09.title: 很
1-09.meaning: 很 means very, but it often just links the subject to an adjective.
1-09.placement: Put 很 right before the adjective.
1-09.english_note: Chinese uses 很 where English just says "is", so no 是 is needed.
1-09.text: 很 means very, but it often just links the subject to an adjective. Put 很 right before the adjective. Chinese uses 很 where English just says "is", so no 是 is needed.

1-09.title: 最
1-09.placement: Put 最 before an adjective or before a verb like 喜欢.
1-09.text: 最 means the most. Put 最 before an adjective or before a verb like 喜欢.

1-09.title: 真
1-09.placement: Put 真 right before the adjective.
1-09.text: 真 means really. Put 真 right before the adjective.

1-09.title: 非常
1-09.placement: Put 非常 right before the adjective.
1-09.text: 非常 means very. Put 非常 right before the adjective.

1-10.title: 一起
1-10.meaning: 一起 means doing something together with other people.
1-10.placement: Put it after the subject and before the verb.
1-10.english_note: English says "together" after the verb, but Chinese puts 一起 before it.
1-10.text: 一起 means doing something together with other people. Put it after the subject and before the verb. English says "together" after the verb, but Chinese puts 一起 before it.

1-10.title: 都
1-10.meaning: 都 means all or both, for more than one person or thing.
1-10.placement: Put it after the subject and before the verb or adjective.
1-10.english_note: English "all" can come first, but 都 never starts the sentence.
1-10.text: 都 means all or both, for more than one person or thing. Put it after the subject and before the verb or adjective. English "all" can come first, but 都 never starts the sentence.

1-11.title: 正在 / 正
1-11.meaning: 正在 means someone is in the middle of doing something at that moment.
1-11.placement: Put it right before the verb.
1-11.english_note: It can mean "is doing" or "was doing", and the verb stays the same.
1-11.text: 正在 means someone is in the middle of doing something at that moment. Put it right before the verb. It can mean "is doing" or "was doing", and the verb stays the same.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing actions in progress (full form) (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGEYQ9O)
AllSet Learning: Expressing actions in progress with "zai" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG846EA)

1-12.title: 常常 / 常
structure: Subj. + 常常 / 常 + Verb + Obj.
1-12.meaning: 常常 means "often", and 常 means the same thing.
1-12.placement: Put it after the subject and before the verb.
1-12.english_note: Don't put it at the start of the sentence.
1-12.text: 常常 means "often", and 常 means the same thing. Put it after the subject and before the verb. Don't put it at the start of the sentence.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "again" in the future with "zai" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGIZQJ2)

1-12.title: 再
structure: 再 + Verb + Number + Measure word + Noun
1-12.meaning: 再 means doing something again, or doing some more.
1-12.english_note: Use it for things that have not happened yet.
1-12.text: 再 means doing something again, or doing some more. Put it before the verb. Use it for things that have not happened yet.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "again" in the future with "zai" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGIZQJ2)

1-13.title: 也
1-13.placement: Put it after the subject and right before the verb.
1-13.english_note: English can say "too" at the end, but Chinese never puts 也 at the end.
1-13.text: 也 means "also" or "too". Put it after the subject and right before the verb. English can say "too" at the end, but Chinese never puts 也 at the end.

1-13.title: 还
structure: 还 + 有 + Number + Measure word + Noun
1-13.meaning: 还 means "more" or "in addition", adding something to what is already there.
1-13.placement: Put it right before the verb.
1-13.text: 还 means "more" or "in addition", adding something to what is already there. Put it right before the verb.

1-14.title: 不
1-14.meaning: 不 means "not" and makes a verb or an adjective negative.
1-14.placement: Put it right before the verb or adjective.
1-14.text: 不 means "not" and makes a verb or an adjective negative. Put it right before the verb or adjective.
sources: AllSet Learning: Negation of past actions with "meiyou" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGAUCXK)

1-14.title: 别
1-14.meaning: 别 means "don't" and tells someone not to do something.
1-14.placement: Put it right before the verb.
1-14.text: 别 means "don't" and tells someone not to do something. Put it right before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Negation of past actions with "meiyou" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGAUCXK)

1-14.title: 没(有)
1-14.meaning: 没(有) means something did not happen, or you do not have something.
1-14.placement: Put it right before the verb or the noun.
1-14.text: 没(有) means something did not happen, or you do not have something. Put it right before the verb or the noun.
sources: AllSet Learning: Negation of past actions with "meiyou" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGAUCXK)

1-15.title: 从
1-15.meaning: 从 means "from" and shows where something starts.
1-15.placement: Put 从 and the place before the verb.
1-15.english_note: English says the verb first ("go from here"), but Chinese puts "from + place" before the verb.
1-15.text: 从 means "from" and shows where something starts. Put 从 and the place before the verb. English says the verb first ("go from here"), but Chinese puts "from + place" before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "from… to…" with "cong… dao…" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGGGIW8)

1-16.title: 在
1-16.meaning: 在 means at, in or on a place.
1-16.placement: Put 在 + place before the verb, use it alone for where something is, or put it after 住 or 坐.
1-16.english_note: English says the place after the verb, but Chinese usually says it before.
1-16.text: 在 means at, in or on a place. Put 在 + place before the verb, use it alone for where something is, or put it after 住 or 坐. English says the place after the verb, but Chinese usually says it before.
sources: AllSet Learning: Special cases of "zai" following verbs (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG90DXK)
AllSet Learning: Expressing location with "zai... shang / xia / li" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGFBWZL)
AllSet Learning: Expressing existence in a place with "zai" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGLRWT8)

1-17.title: 和
1-17.meaning: 和 means "and" and joins two nouns.
1-17.placement: Put it between the two nouns.
1-17.text: 和 means "and" and joins two nouns. Put it between the two nouns.

1-17.title: 跟
1-17.placement: Put 跟 and the person before the verb.
1-17.english_note: English says "with" after the verb, but Chinese puts it before the verb.
1-17.text: 跟 means "with" a person. Put 跟 and the person before the verb. English says "with" after the verb, but Chinese puts it before the verb.

1-18.title: 比
1-18.meaning: 比 means "than" and is used to say one thing is more (tall, cheap, big...) than another.
1-18.placement: Put 比 between the two things you compare, with the adjective at the end.
1-18.english_note: English puts "than" after the adjective, but Chinese puts 比 before it.
1-18.text: 比 means "than" and is used to say one thing is more (tall, cheap, big...) than another. Put 比 between the two things you compare, with the adjective at the end. English puts "than" after the adjective, but Chinese puts 比 before it.

1-19.title: 和
1-19.meaning: 和 means "and" and joins two things.
1-19.placement: Put it between the two nouns.
1-19.text: 和 means "and" and joins two things. Put it between the two nouns.

1-19.title: 跟
1-19.meaning: 跟 means "with" and shows who you do something with.
1-19.placement: Put 跟 and the person before the verb.
1-19.english_note: English puts "with" after the verb, but Chinese puts 跟 before it.
1-19.text: 跟 means "with" and shows who you do something with. Put 跟 and the person before the verb. English puts "with" after the verb, but Chinese puts 跟 before it.

1-20.title: 的

1-22.title: 吗

1-30.title: Subj. + (很) + Adj.
1-30.meaning: Subj. + 很 + Adj. says what someone or something is like.

1-31.title: One-word sentence
1-31.meaning: A one-word sentence like 喂 means a whole message all by itself, with no subject or verb.

1-33.english_note: It does not move to the front like English "what".

1-33.title: 几 (几点)
1-33.meaning: 几点 asks what time it is, or what time something happens.
1-33.placement: Put it after the subject, before the verb.

1-33.title: 怎么了

1-33.title: 哪个
1-33.placement: Put it where the answer would go.
1-33.english_note: It does not move to the front like English "which".

1-33.title: 哪里
1-33.placement: Put it after 在, where the place would go.
1-33.english_note: It stays at the end instead of moving to the front.

1-34.title: 请 + Verb
1-34.meaning: 请 means "please" and politely asks someone to do something.
1-34.placement: Put it at the start of the sentence, right before the verb.
1-34.english_note: You don't need to say "you"; just start with 请.

1-35.title: Exclamation sentence (!)
1-35.meaning: An exclamation sentence shows strong feeling, such as praise, a greeting, or a goodbye.

1-36.title: 是
1-36.meaning: 是 means 'am', 'is' or 'are' and joins two nouns, like 'he is a teacher'.
1-36.placement: Put it between the two nouns, and add 不 before it to say 'is not'.
1-36.english_note: It is used to join nouns, not to describe someone with an adjective.

1-37.title: 有
1-37.meaning: 有 means to have, or that there is or there are something somewhere.

1-37.meaning: 没有 means do not have, or there is not any.
1-37.placement: Put it right before the thing that is missing.

1-38.title: A 比 B + Adj.

1-39.meaning: Sentence 1, Sentence 2 means two short sentences side by side, each saying something about a different person or thing.

2-11.text: 一下 means doing an action briefly or "a little", and it can make the sentence sound softer. Put it right after the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words for verbs (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG5AODR)

2-11.title: 场
2-11.meaning: 场 counts a whole event, such as a movie, a game, or a rainstorm.
2-11.placement: Put it after a number and before the noun.
2-11.text: 场 counts a whole event, such as a movie, a game, or a rainstorm. Put it after a number and before the noun.
sources: AllSet Learning: Measure words for verbs (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG5AODR)

2-12.title: 分钟
structure: Subj. + Verb + 了 + Number + 分钟 + Obj.
2-12.meaning: 分钟 means minutes, and it tells how long something lasts.
2-12.placement: Put it after a number, right after the verb, before the object.
2-12.english_note: Chinese has no word for "for"; the time length just comes after the verb.
2-12.text: 分钟 means minutes, and it tells how long something lasts. Put it after a number, right after the verb, before the object. Chinese has no word for "for"; the time length just comes after the verb.

2-12.title: 年
structure: Subj. + Verb + 了 + Number + 年 + Obj.
2-12.meaning: 年 means years, and it tells how long something lasts.
2-12.placement: Put it after a number, right after the verb, before the object.
2-12.english_note: Chinese has no word for "for"; it needs no extra measure word after the number.
2-12.text: 年 means years, and it tells how long something lasts. Put it after a number, right after the verb, before the object. Chinese has no word for "for"; it needs no extra measure word after the number.

2-12.title: 天
structure: Subj. + Verb + 了 + Number + 天 + Obj.
2-12.meaning: 天 means days, and it tells how long something lasts.
2-12.placement: Put it after a number, right after the verb, before the object.
2-12.english_note: Chinese has no word for "for"; the time length just comes after the verb.
2-12.text: 天 means days, and it tells how long something lasts. Put it after a number, right after the verb, before the object. Chinese has no word for "for"; the time length just comes after the verb.

2-12.title: 周
structure: Subj. + Verb + 了 + Number + 周 + Obj.
2-12.meaning: 周 means weeks, and it tells how long something lasts.
2-12.placement: Put it after a number, right after the verb, before the object.
2-12.english_note: Chinese has no word for "for"; the time length just comes after the verb.
2-12.text: 周 means weeks, and it tells how long something lasts. Put it after a number, right after the verb, before the object. Chinese has no word for "for"; the time length just comes after the verb.

2-13.title: 有(一)点(儿)
2-13.meaning: 有点 means "a bit" and is often used for things you don't like.
2-13.text: 有点 means "a bit" and is often used for things you don't like. Put it before an adjective.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "a little too" with "you dian" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGPM3MY)

2-13.title: 挺
2-13.meaning: 挺 means "quite" or "pretty", as in "pretty good".
2-13.placement: Put it before an adjective, often with 的 at the end.
2-13.text: 挺 means "quite" or "pretty", as in "pretty good". Put it before an adjective, often with 的 at the end.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "a little too" with "you dian" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGPM3MY)

2-13.title: 更
2-13.english_note: Chinese puts 更 before the adjective instead of adding "-er" to it.
2-13.text: 更 means "even more". Put it before an adjective. Chinese puts 更 before the adjective instead of adding "-er" to it.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "a little too" with "you dian" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGPM3MY)

2-13.title: 特别
2-13.text: 特别 means "especially" or "very". Put it before an adjective.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "a little too" with "you dian" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGPM3MY)

2-13.title: 十分
2-13.text: 十分 means "very" or "extremely". Put it before an adjective.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "a little too" with "you dian" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGPM3MY)

2-13.title: 多么
2-13.meaning: 多么 means "how" and shows strong feeling about something.
2-13.placement: Put it before an adjective, often with 啊 at the end.
2-13.english_note: English says "How pretty!" and Chinese uses 多么 the same way.
2-13.text: 多么 means "how" and shows strong feeling about something. Put it before an adjective, often with 啊 at the end. English says "How pretty!" and Chinese uses 多么 the same way.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "a little too" with "you dian" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGPM3MY)

2-13.title: 多
2-13.meaning: 多 means "how" or "so" when you feel strongly about something.
2-13.placement: Put it before an adjective, often with 啊 at the end.
2-13.text: 多 means "how" or "so" when you feel strongly about something. Put it before an adjective, often with 啊 at the end.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "a little too" with "you dian" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGPM3MY)

2-13.title: 好
2-13.meaning: 好 means "so" or "very" in everyday speech.
2-13.english_note: Here 好 is not "good"; it makes the adjective stronger.
2-13.text: 好 means "so" or "very" in everyday speech. Put it before an adjective. Here 好 is not "good"; it makes the adjective stronger.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "a little too" with "you dian" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGPM3MY)

2-14.title: 只
2-14.meaning: 只 means "only" or "just" and shows there is a small amount or no more than that.
2-14.placement: Put it right before the verb.
2-14.text: 只 means "only" or "just" and shows there is a small amount or no more than that. Put it right before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Indicating the whole with "quan" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGCPDSR)

2-15.title: 已经
2-15.meaning: 已经 means something has already happened or is already true.
2-15.placement: Put it before the verb, and put 了 at the end of the sentence.
2-15.text: 已经 means something has already happened or is already true. Put it before the verb, and put 了 at the end of the sentence.

2-16.title: 经常
2-16.meaning: 经常 means something happens often.
2-16.text: 经常 means something happens often. Put it before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Using "always" as a complaint with "laoshi" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGII66E)
AllSet Learning: Expressing "again" in the past with "you" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGN1JR5)

2-17.title: 就
2-17.meaning: 就 means "then": the first part gives a situation, and the second part says what happens or what to do next.
2-17.placement: Put 就 right before the verb in the second part.
2-17.english_note: English often leaves out "then", but Chinese likes to keep 就.
2-17.text: 就 means "then": the first part gives a situation, and the second part says what happens or what to do next. Put 就 right before the verb in the second part. English often leaves out "then", but Chinese likes to keep 就.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "as long as" with "zhiyao" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG98C1A)

2-22.title: 往
2-22.meaning: 往 means "towards" and shows which direction you do something in.
2-22.placement: Put 往 and the direction word before the verb.
2-22.english_note: English puts the direction after the verb ("look up"), but Chinese puts it before.
2-22.text: 往 means "towards" and shows which direction you do something in. Put 往 and the direction word before the verb. English puts the direction after the verb ("look up"), but Chinese puts it before.

2-24.title: 从
2-24.meaning: 从 means "from" and shows where something starts.
2-24.placement: Put 从 + place before the verb.
2-24.english_note: English puts "from" after the verb, but Chinese puts 从 and the place before the verb.
2-24.text: 从 means "from" and shows where something starts. Put 从 + place before the verb. English puts "from" after the verb, but Chinese puts 从 and the place before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "from… to…" with "cong… dao…" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGGGIW8)

2-25.title: 对
2-25.meaning: 对 means "to" or "toward" someone or something, showing who an action or feeling is aimed at.
2-25.placement: Put 对 and the person before the verb or adjective.
2-25.english_note: English says "talk to him", but Chinese puts 对 + person before the verb.
2-25.text: 对 means "to" or "toward" someone or something, showing who an action or feeling is aimed at. Put 对 and the person before the verb or adjective. English says "talk to him", but Chinese puts 对 + person before the verb.

2-26.title: 给
2-26.meaning: 给 means 'to' or 'for' and shows who an action is aimed at.
2-26.placement: Put 给 and the person before the verb.
2-26.english_note: English puts the person after the verb ('call you'), but Chinese puts 给 + person before it.
2-26.text: 给 means 'to' or 'for' and shows who an action is aimed at. Put 给 and the person before the verb. English puts the person after the verb ('call you'), but Chinese puts 给 + person before it.

2-27.title: 离
structure: Place 1 + 离 + Place 2 + 很 + 近/远
2-27.meaning: 离 means 'from' when you say how far or close one place is to another.
2-27.placement: Put it between the two places, before 近 or 远.
2-27.english_note: English puts 'from' after 'far'; Chinese puts 离 before the adjective.
2-27.text: 离 means 'from' when you say how far or close one place is to another. Put it between the two places, before 近 or 远. English puts 'from' after 'far'; Chinese puts 离 before the adjective.

2-30.title: 但 / 但是
2-30.meaning: 但 and 但是 mean "but" and show that the second part goes against the first.
2-30.placement: Put it at the start of the second part, after the first part.
2-30.text: 但 and 但是 mean "but" and show that the second part goes against the first. Put it at the start of the second part, after the first part.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "as long as" with "zhiyao" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG98C1A)
AllSet Learning: Expressing "if... then..." with "ruguo... jiu..." (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGGIVT0)

2-31.title: Verb + 得 + Adj.
structure: Subj. + Verb + 得 + 很 + Adj.
2-31.meaning: 得 links an action to a description of how well or how it is done.
2-31.placement: Put 得 right after the verb, then add the description.
2-31.english_note: English says "slept well" with no extra word; Chinese puts 得 between the verb and the description.
2-31.text: 得 links an action to a description of how well or how it is done. Put 得 right after the verb, then add the description. English says "slept well" with no extra word; Chinese puts 得 between the verb and the description.

2-32.title: Verb + 过
2-32.meaning: 过 means you have done something at least once before, or have had that experience.
2-32.placement: Put it right after the verb.
2-32.english_note: Chinese needs no extra word like "ever" or "before"; 过 does that job.
2-32.text: 过 means you have done something at least once before, or have had that experience. Put it right after the verb. Chinese needs no extra word like "ever" or "before"; 过 does that job.

2-33.title: Verb + 着 + Verb
2-33.meaning: 着 after a verb shows how someone does a second action, like smiling while looking.
2-33.placement: Put 着 right after the first verb, then add the main action verb.
2-33.english_note: English often uses "-ing" or "while" for the first verb.
2-33.text: 着 after a verb shows how someone does a second action, like smiling while looking. Put 着 right after the first verb, then add the main action verb. English often uses "-ing" or "while" for the first verb.

2-34.title: 吧
2-34.meaning: 吧 at the end of a sentence turns it into a friendly suggestion, like "let's" or "how about".
2-34.placement: Put it at the very end of the sentence.
2-34.english_note: English says "let's" at the start; Chinese just adds 吧 at the end, often with 我们.
2-34.text: 吧 at the end of a sentence turns it into a friendly suggestion, like "let's" or "how about". Put it at the very end of the sentence. English says "let's" at the start; Chinese just adds 吧 at the end, often with 我们.

2-36.title: 喂
2-36.meaning: 喂 means "hello" and is used to start or answer a phone call.
2-36.placement: Put it at the very start, before what you say next.
2-36.english_note: 喂 is mainly for phone calls, not for greeting people face to face.
2-36.text: 喂 means "hello" and is used to start or answer a phone call. Put it at the very start, before what you say next. 喂 is mainly for phone calls, not for greeting people face to face.

2-43.title: 什么的
2-43.meaning: 什么的 means "and so on" and ends a list of things.
2-43.placement: Put it at the end of the list, after the last item.
2-43.english_note: English says "and so on" after the list too, but 什么的 is more casual.
2-43.text: 什么的 means "and so on" and ends a list of things. Put it at the end of the list, after the last item. English says "and so on" after the list too, but 什么的 is more casual.
sources: AllSet Learning: Ending a non-exhaustive list with "shenme de" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGDIDAC)

2-45.title: 还是……吧
structure: Subj. + 还是 + Verb + Obj. + 吧
2-45.meaning: 还是……吧 means "had better": you compare the choices and suggest the better one.
2-45.placement: Put 还是 before the verb and 吧 at the end of the sentence.
2-45.english_note: Chinese uses 还是 and 吧 together where English says "had better" or "let's".
2-45.text: 还是……吧 means "had better": you compare the choices and suggest the better one. Put 还是 before the verb and 吧 at the end of the sentence. Chinese uses 还是 and 吧 together where English says "had better" or "let's".

2-48.title: Noun/number phrase as sentence
2-48.meaning: A noun or number phrase can be the main part of a sentence, telling the time, date, weather or amount.
2-48.placement: Put it right after the subject, with no 是.
2-48.english_note: English needs "is" here, but Chinese often leaves it out.
2-48.text: A noun or number phrase can be the main part of a sentence, telling the time, date, weather or amount. Put it right after the subject, with no 是. English needs "is" here, but Chinese often leaves it out.

2-49.title: Verb + 好
2-49.meaning: Verb + 好 means the action is done well or done completely.
2-49.placement: Put 好 right after the verb.
2-49.english_note: English uses a separate word like "well"; Chinese attaches 好 straight to the verb.
2-49.text: Verb + 好 means the action is done well or done completely. Put 好 right after the verb. English uses a separate word like "well"; Chinese attaches 好 straight to the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Result complement "-wan" for finishing (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGNQUC1)

2-49.title: Verb + 晚
2-49.meaning: Verb + 晚 means the action happened too late.
2-49.placement: Put 晚 right after the verb.
2-49.english_note: English says "late" after the verb too, but Chinese joins 晚 directly to the verb.
2-49.text: Verb + 晚 means the action happened too late. Put 晚 right after the verb. English says "late" after the verb too, but Chinese joins 晚 directly to the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Result complement "-wan" for finishing (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGNQUC1)

2-50.title: Verb + 来/去
structure: Subj. + Verb + 上/下 + 来/去
2-50.meaning: Verb + 来/去 shows which way an action goes: 来 is toward the speaker, 去 is away from the speaker.
2-50.placement: Add 上 or 下 before 来/去 to also say up or down.
2-50.text: Verb + 来/去 shows which way an action goes: 来 is toward the speaker, 去 is away from the speaker. Add 上 or 下 before 来/去 to also say up or down.

2-51.title: Verb + 得 + Adj.
structure: Subj. + Verb + 得 + 很 + Adj.
2-51.meaning: Verb + 得 + Adj. tells how well or in what way someone does an action.
2-51.placement: Put 得 right after the verb, then the adjective, usually with 很 before it.
2-51.english_note: English puts 'well' or 'fast' after the action as a separate word; Chinese joins it to the verb with 得.
2-51.text: Verb + 得 + Adj. tells how well or in what way someone does an action. Put 得 right after the verb, then the adjective, usually with 很 before it. English puts 'well' or 'fast' after the action as a separate word; Chinese joins it to the verb with 得.

2-52.title: Verb + 一下(儿)
2-52.meaning: 一下(儿) means doing an action briefly or just a little, and it makes the request or suggestion softer.
2-52.placement: Put it right after the verb, before the object.
2-52.text: 一下(儿) means doing an action briefly or just a little, and it makes the request or suggestion softer. Put it right after the verb, before the object.

2-53.title: Adj. + 一点(儿)
2-53.meaning: 一点儿 means a little, and after an adjective it means a little more of that quality.
2-53.placement: Put it right after the adjective.
2-53.english_note: Where English changes the adjective (quicker, better), Chinese keeps the adjective the same and adds 一点儿.
2-53.text: 一点儿 means a little, and after an adjective it means a little more of that quality. Put it right after the adjective. Where English changes the adjective (quicker, better), Chinese keeps the adjective the same and adds 一点儿.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "age difference" with "da and xiao" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGE8810)
AllSet Learning: Expressing "much more" in comparisons (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG6KUS5)

2-54.title: Noun as the statement
2-54.meaning: Noun + Noun means the second noun tells what the subject is, with no 是 needed.
2-54.english_note: English needs "is", but here the noun can follow the subject directly.
2-54.text: Noun + Noun means the second noun tells what the subject is, with no 是 needed. English needs "is", but here the noun can follow the subject directly.

2-55.title: 有 + amount
structure: Subj. + 有 + Number + Measure word + Adj.
Subj. + 有 + Number + 多 + 岁
2-55.meaning: 有 means someone or something reaches a certain amount, like a height or an age.
2-55.placement: Put it after the subject, right before the number.
2-55.english_note: Where English says "is" (he is 1.8 meters tall), Chinese uses 有.
2-55.text: 有 means someone or something reaches a certain amount, like a height or an age. Put it after the subject, right before the number. Where English says "is" (he is 1.8 meters tall), Chinese uses 有.

2-56.title: Place + Verb + 着 + Noun
2-56.meaning: 着 after a verb means someone or something is there in that state, like sitting or standing.
2-56.placement: Put the place first, then the verb with 着, then who or what is there.
2-56.english_note: English says "There is...", but Chinese just starts with the place.
2-56.text: 着 after a verb means someone or something is there in that state, like sitting or standing. Put the place first, then the verb with 着, then who or what is there. English says "There is...", but Chinese just starts with the place.

2-57.title: Verb + Obj. + Verb + Obj.
structure: Subj. + 坐 + Noun + 去 + Place
2-57.meaning: Verb + Obj. + Verb + Obj. means two actions happen one after the other.
2-57.placement: Say the first action first, then the second, both after the subject.
2-57.english_note: Chinese needs no "and" or "to" between the two actions.
2-57.text: Verb + Obj. + Verb + Obj. means two actions happen one after the other. Say the first action first, then the second, both after the subject. Chinese needs no "and" or "to" between the two actions.

2-58.title: 比
2-58.meaning: 比 means "than" and compares two things.
2-58.placement: Put it between the two things, with the adjective after the second one.
2-58.english_note: English puts "than" after the adjective, but 比 comes before it.
2-58.text: 比 means "than" and compares two things. Put it between the two things, with the adjective after the second one. English puts "than" after the adjective, but 比 comes before it.
sources: AllSet Learning: Expressing "much more" in comparisons (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG6KUS5)
AllSet Learning: Expressing "age difference" with "da and xiao" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGE8810)

2-60.title: 是……的
structure: Subj. + 是 + Time/Place/Way + Verb + 的
Subj. + 是 + 在 + Place + Verb + 的
2-60.meaning: 是……的 points out a detail of something that already happened, like when, where or how.
2-60.placement: Put the detail right after 是, and put 的 at the end of the sentence.
2-60.english_note: English stresses the detail with its voice, but Chinese puts it between 是 and 的.
2-60.text: 是……的 points out a detail of something that already happened, like when, where or how. Put the detail right after 是, and put 的 at the end of the sentence. English stresses the detail with its voice, but Chinese puts it between 是 and 的.
sources: AllSet Learning: The "shi... de" construction for emphasizing details (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGE662E)
AllSet Learning: The "shi... de" patterns: an overview (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG8YTSF)

2-61.title: Verb + person + thing
2-61.meaning: Verb + person + thing means someone gives, tells or teaches a person something, using verbs like 给, 教 and 告诉.
2-61.placement: Put the person right after the verb, then the thing.
2-61.english_note: No word like "to" goes between them.
2-61.text: Verb + person + thing means someone gives, tells or teaches a person something, using verbs like 给, 教 and 告诉. Put the person right after the verb, then the thing. No word like "to" goes between them.

2-64.title: A,还是 B?
structure: Subj. + Verb + Noun 1 + 还是 + Verb + Noun 2?
2-64.meaning: 还是 means "or" when you ask someone to pick one of two choices.
2-64.placement: Put it between the two choices, and end the whole sentence as a question.
2-64.english_note: The question does not need 吗.
2-64.text: 还是 means "or" when you ask someone to pick one of two choices. Put it between the two choices, and end the whole sentence as a question. The question does not need 吗.

2-65.title: 但(是)
2-65.meaning: 但 and 但是 mean "but" and show that the second part goes against the first part.
2-65.placement: Put it at the start of the second part, after a comma.
2-65.text: 但 and 但是 mean "but" and show that the second part goes against the first part. Put it at the start of the second part, after a comma.

2-68.title: 因为……所以……
structure: 因为 + Reason, 所以 + Result
2-68.meaning: 因为……所以…… means "because ... so ..." and links a reason to its result.
2-68.placement: Put 因为 before the reason, then 所以 before the result.
2-68.english_note: Chinese uses both words in one sentence, but English uses only one of "because" or "so".
2-68.text: 因为……所以…… means "because ... so ..." and links a reason to its result. Put 因为 before the reason, then 所以 before the result. Chinese uses both words in one sentence, but English uses only one of "because" or "so".
sources: AllSet Learning: Cause and effect with "yinwei" and "suoyi" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGTDUJO)

2-69.title: 一……就……
structure: Subj. + 一 + Verb, + 就 + Verb + Obj.
2-69.meaning: 一……就…… means as soon as one thing happens, the next thing happens right after.
2-69.placement: Put 一 before the first verb and 就 before the second verb.
2-69.english_note: English says "as soon as" once, but Chinese uses both 一 and 就.
2-69.text: 一……就…… means as soon as one thing happens, the next thing happens right after. Put 一 before the first verb and 就 before the second verb. English says "as soon as" once, but Chinese uses both 一 and 就.
sources: AllSet Learning: Events in quick succession with "yi... jiu..." (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGTFUD0)

2-70.title: Verb + 着
2-70.meaning: Verb + 着 means an action or state is continuing, like "smiling" or "standing".
2-70.placement: Put 着 right after the verb, and a second verb can follow to show what else is happening.
2-70.english_note: English uses "-ing" or "while"; Chinese just adds 着 after the first verb.
2-70.text: Verb + 着 means an action or state is continuing, like "smiling" or "standing". Put 着 right after the verb, and a second verb can follow to show what else is happening. English uses "-ing" or "while"; Chinese just adds 着 after the first verb.

2-71.title: Verb + 过
structure: Subj. + 没(有) + Verb + 过 + Obj.
2-71.meaning: Verb + 过 means you have done this before, at some time in the past.
2-71.placement: Put 过 right after the verb, before the object.
2-71.english_note: English says "have done"; Chinese just adds 过 after the verb and the verb does not change.
2-71.text: Verb + 过 means you have done this before, at some time in the past. Put 过 right after the verb, before the object. English says "have done"; Chinese just adds 过 after the verb and the verb does not change.

2-72.title: 第 + Number
structure: Subj. + 是 + 第 + Number + Measure word
2-72.meaning: 第 turns a number into 'first', 'second', 'third' and so on.
2-72.placement: Put 第 right before the number, then add a measure word such as 次.
2-72.english_note: Chinese uses 第 for every number, with no endings like -st, -nd or -th.
2-72.text: 第 turns a number into 'first', 'second', 'third' and so on. Put 第 right before the number, then add a measure word such as 次. Chinese uses 第 for every number, with no endings like -st, -nd or -th.

2-73.title: Number + 多
2-73.meaning: 多 after a number means "more than" that number.
2-73.placement: Put it right after a number like 十, 百 or 千, before the measure word.
2-73.english_note: English says "more than" before the number, but Chinese puts 多 after it.
2-73.text: 多 after a number means "more than" that number. Put it right after a number like 十, 百 or 千, before the measure word. English says "more than" before the number, but Chinese puts 多 after it.
sources: AllSet Learning: Indicating a number in excess (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG004ZK)

2-73.title: 几
structure: 几 + 十/百/千/万 + Measure word + Noun
2-73.meaning: 几 means "a few" and is not an exact number.
2-73.placement: Put it before a measure word, or after it add 十, 百, 千 or 万 for "a few tens, hundreds…".
2-73.english_note: Chinese needs a measure word after 几.
2-73.text: 几 means "a few" and is not an exact number. Put it before a measure word, or after it add 十, 百, 千 or 万 for "a few tens, hundreds…". Chinese needs a measure word after 几.
sources: AllSet Learning: Indicating a number in excess (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG004ZK)

2-73.title: 左右
structure: Subj. + Verb + Number + Measure word + 左右 (+ Noun)
2-73.meaning: 左右 means "about" or "around" the number before it.
2-73.placement: Put it after the number and its measure word.
2-73.english_note: English says "about" before the number, but Chinese puts 左右 after it.
2-73.text: 左右 means "about" or "around" the number before it. Put it after the number and its measure word. English says "about" before the number, but Chinese puts 左右 after it.
sources: AllSet Learning: Indicating a number in excess (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASG004ZK)

2-74.title: 就 / 就是
2-74.meaning: 就 means "exactly" or "right", and it stresses that something is just as you say.
2-74.placement: Put it right before 是 or 在, after the subject.
2-74.english_note: English shows this by stressing a word, like "right here" or "exactly"; Chinese adds 就.
2-74.text: 就 means "exactly" or "right", and it stresses that something is just as you say. Put it right before 是 or 在, after the subject. English shows this by stressing a word, like "right here" or "exactly"; Chinese adds 就.

2-75.title: 好吗
2-75.meaning: 好吗 asks if the other person agrees with your idea or request.
2-75.placement: Say your idea first, then put 好吗 at the very end.
2-75.english_note: It works like "OK?" added to the end of an English sentence.
2-75.text: 好吗 asks if the other person agrees with your idea or request. Say your idea first, then put 好吗 at the very end. It works like "OK?" added to the end of an English sentence.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)

2-75.title: 可以吗
2-75.meaning: 可以吗 asks if something is allowed or fine with the other person.
2-75.placement: Say what you want to do first, then put 可以吗 at the very end.
2-75.english_note: It works like "Is that OK?" or "May I?" added to the end.

sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)

2-75.title: 行吗
2-75.meaning: 行吗 asks if something is OK with the other person.
2-75.placement: Say your idea first, then put 行吗 at the very end.
2-75.english_note: It works like "OK?" added to the end of an English sentence.
2-75.text: 行吗 asks if something is OK with the other person. Say your idea first, then put 行吗 at the very end. It works like "OK?" added to the end of an English sentence.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)

2-75.title: 怎么样
structure: 你觉得 + Noun + 怎么样？
2-75.meaning: 怎么样 asks how something is or what it is like.
2-75.placement: Put the thing you ask about first, then 怎么样 at the end.
2-75.english_note: English starts with "how", but 怎么样 comes last, and it needs no 吗.
2-75.text: 怎么样 asks how something is or what it is like. Put the thing you ask about first, then 怎么样 at the end. English starts with "how", but 怎么样 comes last, and it needs no 吗.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)

2-76.title: 什么时候
structure: Subj. + 什么时候 + Verb + Obj. ?
2-76.meaning: 什么时候 means "when" and asks about time.
2-76.placement: It goes where the time word would go, usually after the subject.
2-76.english_note: English puts "when" first, but Chinese keeps it in the normal time spot.
2-76.text: 什么时候 means "when" and asks about time. It goes where the time word would go, usually after the subject. English puts "when" first, but Chinese keeps it in the normal time spot.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)

2-76.title: 什么样
structure: Subj. + Verb + 什么样 + 的 + Noun ?
2-76.meaning: 什么样 means "what kind of" and asks about the type or look of something.
2-76.placement: Put it before 的 and a noun, in the spot where the noun would be.
2-76.english_note: English moves "what kind of" to the front, but Chinese keeps it in the object's spot.
2-76.text: 什么样 means "what kind of" and asks about the type or look of something. Put it before 的 and a noun, in the spot where the noun would be. English moves "what kind of" to the front, but Chinese keeps it in the object's spot.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)

2-76.title: 为什么
2-76.meaning: 为什么 means "why" and asks for a reason.
2-76.placement: It usually goes at the start or right before the verb.
2-76.text: 为什么 means "why" and asks for a reason. It usually goes at the start or right before the verb.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)

2-76.title: 怎么样
structure: 你觉得 + Noun + 怎么样 ?
2-76.meaning: 怎么样 means "how is it?" and is a question about what something is like.
2-76.placement: It goes at the end, right after the thing you are asking about.
2-76.english_note: Chinese needs no word for "is" here; just put 怎么样 after the topic.
2-76.text: 怎么样 means "how is it?" and is a question about what something is like. It goes at the end, right after the thing you are asking about. Chinese needs no word for "is" here; just put 怎么样 after the topic.
sources: AllSet Learning: Asking how something is with "zenmeyang" (https://resources.allsetlearning.com/chinese/grammar/ASGC701A)

2-76.title: 怎样
2-76.meaning: 怎样 means "how" and asks what something is like.
2-76.placement: It usually goes after the thing you are asking about.
2-76.english_note: Chinese needs no word for "is" here; just put 怎样 after the topic.

2-77.title: Noun + 呢？
2-77.meaning: 呢 means "what about...?" and asks a question about the person or thing right before it.
2-77.placement: Say the person or thing first, then put 呢 at the end.
2-77.english_note: Chinese needs no words for "what about"; 呢 does that job.
2-77.text: 呢 means "what about...?" and asks a question about the person or thing right before it. Say the person or thing first, then put 呢 at the end. Chinese needs no words for "what about"; 呢 does that job.

2-78.title: 是不是
2-78.meaning: 是不是 turns a sentence into a question that asks "is it so or not?"
2-78.placement: Put it right before the noun or phrase you are asking about, in place of 是.
2-78.english_note: English uses "Is he...?" or "...or not?", but Chinese puts 是 and 不是 together.
2-78.text: 是不是 turns a sentence into a question that asks "is it so or not?" Put it right before the noun or phrase you are asking about, in place of 是. English uses "Is he...?" or "...or not?", but Chinese puts 是 and 不是 together.

2-79.title: Statement + 吧?
2-79.meaning: Statement + 吧? means you guess something is true and want the other person to confirm it.
2-79.placement: Put 吧 at the end of the sentence.
2-79.english_note: English uses a tag like "right?" or "isn't it?", but Chinese just adds 吧 at the end.
2-79.text: Statement + 吧? means you guess something is true and want the other person to confirm it. Put 吧 at the end of the sentence. English uses a tag like "right?" or "isn't it?", but Chinese just adds 吧 at the end.

2-81.title: 快要……了
2-81.meaning: 快要 means something is about to happen very soon.
2-81.placement: Put 快要 before the verb and 了 at the end.
2-81.english_note: English has no word like 了 to close the sentence, but Chinese uses it here.
2-81.text: 快要 means something is about to happen very soon. Put 快要 before the verb and 了 at the end. English has no word like 了 to close the sentence, but Chinese uses it here.

2-81.title: 就要……了
structure: Subj. + Time + 就要 + Verb + 了
2-81.meaning: 就要 means something is about to happen soon, and it can go with a time like next month.
2-81.placement: Put the time first, then 就要 before the verb, and 了 at the end.
2-81.text: 就要 means something is about to happen soon, and it can go with a time like next month. Put the time first, then 就要 before the verb, and 了 at the end.

x-erhua.title: 哪儿

x-erhua.placement: Put it where the place would go in the answer.
x-erhua.english_note: It stays in the same spot as the answer, not at the start of the sentence.

x-erhua.title: 玩儿

x-erhua.placement: Put it after the subject, with a place before it if you need one.
